note: ERA 11. T7 (A70): five cheap rows - clinic, policeHQ, fireHQ, reservoir, wasteFacility - and five deputy considerations, which is why this is an era rather than a catalogue edit. The clinic is the only health a young town can afford and the deputy builds one per deputy.buildingsPerClinic; the headquarters are one-offs past headquartersAtPopulation; the reservoir replaces the pump past reservoirAtPopulation; the tip is built once the city is tipAtPopulation big AND its pollution over developed land passes tipAtPollution (5, which is what the sweep actually reports - the first cut guessed 24 and only ever fired in a village, where two power stations and nine houses is a filthy city by that measure, and it bankrupted every town it fired in: seed 1003 peaked at SIXTY people against 1,260 without it). Measured with tools/sim_sweep.mjs over 200 games per configuration; see reports/balance-era11.md. ERA 10. T6 (A67, A70): leisure and education are coverage layers of their own - tiles.leisure and tiles.education, hashed and saved - fed by five new definitions (plaza, library, stadium, school, university) plus the park and the marina, with a funding row each. They reach the city twice: civic.amenityValueDivisor adds them to land value beside the three departments, and civic.amenityDemand puts the average over DEVELOPED land into the residential pool. The deputy builds a school every deputy.buildingsPerSchool buildings and a plaza every buildingsPerPlaza, so a headless city has both - without that every sweep in the project would have measured a town that reads zero on two of the five layers. Re-measured with tools/sim_sweep.mjs over 200 games per configuration; see reports/balance-era10.md. ERA 9. P87 re-mixed the deputy's OWN stream - Math.imul(seat, 0x9e3779b1) ^ index where era 8 had (seat << 20) + index - inside a review round that changed no rule, and nobody re-ran the sweep. Every deputy decision in every city moved with it, so era 8's report describes a set of worlds that no longer exists: measured at 60 games a side, relaxed's median population went 2275 to 2477, steady's 2415 to 2318, and one steady city died. Re-measured with tools/sim_sweep.mjs over 200 games per configuration; see reports/balance-era9.md. No rule changed; every number moved because the worlds did, which is exactly what era 8 said about itself. T5a arrived in the same commit and is not in it: gate.air and airport.maxDrop are ERA 0, UNTUNED and reach nothing a deputy builds - proved by 60 games a side with and without T5a coming back byte-identical. Numbers from era 8 are void, not roughly comparable. ERA 8. Q113: the deputy draws from its OWN stream, a pure function of the seed, the tick, the seat and the draw's index within the turn, instead of from state.rng - which development, fire and disasters also draw from. One extra deputy action used to shift when every later fire started and every later building grew, so a sweep comparing two eras compared two worlds rather than two rules. No rule changed; every number below moved because the worlds did. ERA 7. T4 (A67, A68): water bodies are derived - a flood over the water layer giving each body a size and whether it reaches a map edge - and three buildings hang off them. A marina needs harbour.marinaMinBody tiles of one body beside it. A ferryTerminal and a freightPort are SEA gates: buildable anywhere a marina is, and LIVE only where the body reaches an edge, which is what gate.sea's terms, its fare and its commuter sink follow. The deputy builds a marina and a terminal past deputy.harbourAtPopulation. ERA 6. T2 (A65, A66, A79): rail is a network of its own, a railStation is a GATE, and worldgen places rock and marsh. A live gate - a station whose line reaches a map edge, powered and with road access - adds gate.rail's integer terms to the regional demand pool, seeds the commuter field as a sink and takes gate.rail.farePerResident from every resident within gate.rail.range. build.rail and upkeep.rail are the line's. ERA 5. T1a (A60): a second road kind. An avenue carries traffic.avenueCapacity times a road before it reads as full, and the commuter field crosses it at traffic.avenueStep against a road traffic.roadStep - so a grid with one avenue routes onto it. build.avenue is its price. ERA 4. B1a (A62): a fire nobody fights spreads and burns slowly rather than dying with the house it started in (fire.unfoughtPercent, unfoughtSpread, unfoughtDamage), and the deputy builds a fire station per deputy.buildingsPerStation buildings - until now it built none, and no gate city in the project has ever had a fire service. Era 3: B9 (A81): the deputy lays a road only within deputy.roadReach tiles of a lot that is built, or zoned and supplied, so a played town grows outward and has an edge; see reports/balance-era3.md. Era 2 is left to T1/T2's re-pin (A79). Otherwise unchanged from era 1 — ERA 1. Tuned 2026-08-29 against tools/sim_sweep.mjs over 200 games per configuration; see reports/balance-era1.md. Changed from era 0: civic.pollutionAverage now averages over developed land instead of the whole region, so it reads 9 instead of 0 and can drive something. RE-TESTED AND REJECTED, for the second time: per-tile wire and pipe upkeep. At 1 each it put p25 treasury on 0 and cut p25 population from 647 to 187 — it bankrupts weak cities without touching the rich ones, which is what the era-0 note already said. ACCEPTED, not fixed: runaway treasuries, median 1.9M and p95 3.8M after 25 years. Numbers from era 0 are void, not roughly comparable.

gate._comment: T2 (A65): the Outside is gate buildings, not a second simulation. A LIVE gate adds these integer terms to the regional demand pool, seeds the commuter field as a sink, and takes a fare from every resident within range. ERA 0, UNTUNED against the bases in `demand` below (400/150/150).

air._comment: T5 (A69): the largest terms there are, plus a LANDING FEE - a flat monthly sum a live airport earns from the aircraft rather than from the residents near it, which is why an airport in an empty region is still worth something. ERA 0, UNTUNED.

airport._comment: T5 (A69). maxDrop is the largest difference in `tiles.elevation` the airport's footprint may contain - a runway is flat, and the engine has no metres. Six units is three metres at the renderer's half-metre relief step, a tenth of the grade a road is allowed over the same 120 m, because a road climbs and a runway does not. On a rolling map about one 6x4 site in ten qualifies; on a hilly one almost none, which is the intent.

harbour._comment: T4 (A67, A68). marinaMinBody is how many tiles of one body a marina needs beside it - a pond is not a harbour. `water` next to this is the UTILITY's, and a second block of that name silently replaced it. ERA 0, UNTUNED.

fire._unfought: B1a (A62): a fire is unaddressed when at least unfoughtPercent of the building's own fire risk is left after coverage - no station in range - and it then spreads unfoughtSpread times as readily while consuming its house more slowly, so it outlives what it is standing on and reaches the next one.

disasters._comment: era 0, untuned. Frequency is difficulty.disasterOneIn, which already existed; this is only the shape of one.

traffic._comment: era 0, untuned. roadCapacity is load units per tile before a street reads as full.

deputy._comment: A81 (B9): the deputy lays a road only within roadReach tiles of a lot that is built, or zoned and supplied; expand reaches a little further than the doctrines that hold back. Era 3. T2: railAtPopulation is the size at which it lays a line to the edge and puts a station on it - just above avenueAtPopulation, so the order is the main road first and the railway after it.
